Explaining further, the Department informed that ou t of 2140 employees, only 78 had 
indicated their intention to continue with JIPMER, 76 had opted to continue with the 
Central Government while the remaining 1986 employe es had not exercised their 
option so far. It was also stated that most of the employees had made up their mind 
and for those who had not given their option, they would be absorbed in the Institute 
automatically. It was pointed out that since the ex tension of time proposed in the 
amendment is a one-time affair, this chapter would be given a successful conclusion 
by January, 2011 i.e. the time by when the extensio n of two and one-half years would 
end.  
 
12.    Director of JIPMER, who was also present in the meeting, apprised the 
Committee that majority of the faculty members had decided to stay with the Institute 
and about 20 among them wishing to continue as Cent ral Government Health Service 
Employees had been already transferred. The Committ ee was given to understand 

 11  
that the element of indecision mainly involved Grou p ‘C’ and ‘D’ employees. They 
did not want to leave the Institute as they had bee n settled in Puducherry for a 
considerable period of time and by opting for remai ning with Central Government, 
they were liable to be transferred. At the same tim e, benefits as Central Government 
employees were also proving to be very attractive. Lack of clarity of applicability of 
such benefits to the Institute employees had resulted in such a conflicting scenario. He 
cited the case of 40 nurses who had opted to remain  as Central Government 
employees earlier and were now worried that they wo uld be transferred out of 
Puducherry. The amendment would also give an opportunity to those employees who 
had already exercised their option but not transfer red out of the Institute to exercise 
their option afresh. It was pointed out that most o f the nurses who wished to be given 
a chance to revisit their decision were senior nurs es who were presently working at 
the Institute. Not only these nurses would be a sat isfied lot but the Institute would 
also stand to gain from their rich experience if they were allowed to stay back.  
 
13.    On a specific query about the apprehensions of the employees regarding 
pensionary benefits, it was informed that the matter was taken up with the 
Department of Personnel and Training, Pensions and Administrative Reforms to 
ensure grant of pensionary benefits to JIPMER employees under Rule 37 (A) as 
was done in erstwhile Departments of Government of India like the Department of 
Telecommunication when it was converted into BSNL. However, the Department’s 
proposal to amend the pension rule to facilitate the JIPMER employees to get their 
pension from the Consolidated Fund of India was rejected by DOPT on the ground 
that enough safeguards had already been made available to the employees and 
hence it felt that there could not be any justification for considering the proposal 
on the lines of BSNL employees. 
 
14. With regard to the employees’ suggestion regard ing inclusion of Central 
Administrative Tribunal (CAT) as the appellate auth ority for grievance redressal, the 
Department stated that the issue had already been r esolved and a formal notification 

 12  
would be issued by the DoPT. It was clarified by th e Department that all the 
employees of JIPMER would be getting additional fac ilities after the enactment of 
JIPMER Act. The Committee was also given to underst and that pay structure of 
JIPMER doctors would be the same as given to doctor s at AIIMS and PGIMER, 
Chandigarh. Not only this, as decided in the first Standing Finance Committee of the 
Institute, allowances given to JIPMER doctors would  be at par with those given to 
AIIMS and PGIMER doctors. 
 
 15.      Taking into account the entire gamut of i ssues surrounding Section 28 of 
the JIPMER Act, 2008, the Committee has the following observations to make:-  
 
15.1 The Committee stands by its observation that a  period of one year should 
have been sufficient for exercising of option by th e employees as to whether they 
wanted to remain as employees of JIPMER or to conti nue as employees of Central 
Government. The Committee finds that the apprehensi ons of the employees 
regarding the pensionary benefits as well as other conditions of service are 
adequately covered under Regulations 41 and 43 of t he JIPMER, Puducherry 
Regulations, 2008 as notified on the 4 
th  August 2008 in the Gazette of India. With 
regulations also being notified as early as on the 4 th  August 2008, within a very 
short span of 20 days after the enactment of the Ac t, the Committee fails to 
comprehend the reasons for the element of indecisio n persisting for such a long 
time. The Committee observes that if the Ministry h ad been explicit in providing 
this information to the employees at the outset alo ng with Institute authorities 
playing a pro-active role, it would have been a different story today.  
 
15.2 Another area of concern for the Committee is t he inordinate delay in getting 
such a simple amendment proposal cleared from the M inistry of Law. It speaks 
volumes of the laid back manner in which the entire  matter was dealt with by the 
nodal Ministry and is indicative of lack of proper inter-ministerial coordination. 
Not only this, the Committee is constrained to obse rve that with 1986 employees 

 13  
out of a total of 2140 employees of the Institute c ontinuing to remain undecided, 
functioning of the Institute must also be somewhat adversely affected. 
 
15.3 The Committee would also like to mention here that it has been three years 
since the Committee had presented its report on the  JIPMER, Puducherry Bill, 2007 
to the Parliament. The recommendation of the Commit tee relating to incorporation 
of provision in the Act relating to CAT as the appe llate authority should have been 
settled with the Department of Personnel and Traini ng much earlier. During 
evidence at its meeting held on the 27 
th  September 2010, the representatives of the 
Department had informed the Committee that the issu e relating to CAT had been 
cleared. However, the notification regarding the sa me was yet to come out. The 
Committee safely concludes from the above that the issues have been cleared only 
recently.  The Committee is of the view that the no tification regarding the CAT as 
appellate authority for JIPMER employees needs to b e published at the earliest so 
as to bring more clarity in the matter and dispel a ny further doubts of the 
employees.  
 
15.4 The Committee, after analyzing the entire gamu t of the issues surrounding 
the proposed amendment and taking into account the welfare of the employees and 
the public interest at large and also given the acu te shortage of trained skilled and 
experienced healthcare personnel in government hosp itals across the country, 
approves the amendment to extend the time-period fr om “one year” to “two and 
one-half years”, as proposed in the Bill.

STA TEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS
The Jawaharlal Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry
was declared as an institution of national importance by the Jawaharlal Institute of Post-
Graduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry Act, 2008. The Act was brought into
force on the 14th July, 2008 by the Central Government under sub-section (2) of section 1 of
the Act.
2. Prior to its incorporation as an autonomous body under section 4 of the aforesaid
Act, the Institute was functioning as an institution under the Ministry of Health and Family
Welfare. Hence, on the incorporation of the institution, every employee of the Institute prior
to its conversion was given option under sub-section (1) of section 28 of the aforesaid Act
to exercise his or her option within a period of one year from the date of commencement of the
Act either to remain as an employee of the autonomous Institute or to opt out of the Institute
and continue to remain as a Central Government employee. A number of employees of the
institution have already exercised their option in terms of sub-section (1) of section 28 of the
aforesaid Act. However, a total number of about 1241 representations from Group B, C and D
employees have been received in the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare requesting for
extension of the period for exercising the option to two years from the existing one year as
provided by the said Act. Majority of the employees working in the Institute have not so far
exercised their option.
3. In order to avoid any discrimination and to provide equal opportunity to all the
employees, it has been decided to extend the benefit of enhanced option period from the
existing one year to two and one-half years including those employees who have already
exercised their option and to allow them to exercise option afresh. However, due to practical
reasons this benefit of extension of time may be limited to only those employees who have
not been transferred out of the Institute consequent upon the exercise of option by them.
4. It is proposed to amend sub-section (1) of section 28 of the aforesaid Act for
extending the period of exercising option by the erstwhile employees of the Institute to two
and one-half years from the existing one year from 14th July, 2008 i.e., the date on which the
provisions of the Act came into force. The proposed amendment will enable more time to the
employees of the erstwhile institution to exercise their option either to remain as the employees
of the new autonomous Institute or to opt out of the Institute and continue to remain as
Central Government employees.
5. The Bill seeks to achieve the above objects.

REPORT 
  
 The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the 
recommendations/Observations contained in its Forty-First Report  on Demands for Grants 
(Demand No. 48) of the Department of Health Research for the year 2010-11. 
 
2. Action Taken Notes have been received from the Government in respect of the 
recommendations contained in the Report.  They have been categorized as follows: 
 
(i) Recommendations/ Observations in resp ect of which replies of the Government 
have been accepted by the Committee: 2.15, 3.7, 3.21, 3.22, 3.25, 5.3, 12.5,      
Total – 7                                                                                         (Chapter I)
        
(ii) Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue 
in view of the Government’s  replies: 1.5, 3.15, 3.16, 3.17, 3.18, 3.23, 4.1, 4.2, 
4.3, 8.4, 12.7    Total –11                                                             (Chapter II)
    
(iii) Recommendations/Observations in respect of which re plies of the Government 
have not been accepted by the Committee:  1.3, 1.4, 1.6, 2.2, 2.6, 2.7, 2.8, 2.12, 
2.13, 3.14, 6.2, 6.3, 7.5, 7.6, 9.5, 9.6, 9.7, 9.8, 10.3, 10.4, 10.5, 10.6, 11.3, 13.2, 
14.8  Total –  25                                                                         (Chapter III)
            
(iv) Recommendations/Obser vations in respect of which final replies of the 
Government are still awaited:   - Nil -                                       (Chapter-IV)
    
 
 
 

 CHAPTER-I 
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF 
THE GOVERNMENT HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE 
 
 
II. BUDGETARY ALLOCATION 
 
Recommendations/Observations  
 
2.15 The Committee welcomes the enhanced a llocation for the North Eastern Areas 
for 2010-11, which is fully justified in view of  the excellent track-record of the Region 
in the matter of utilization of the funds allocated in the past. However the Committee 
would like to be enlightened as to whether the entire budget allocation was spent for 
the intended purposes during 2008-09 and 2009- 10 or some part of it was transferred 
to the non-lapsable pool to be utilized later.  
 
Action Taken 
 
Regarding the utilisation of the budget a llocation in the North Eastern areas, it 
is clarified that budget allocated was spent for the intended purpose and not 
transferred to the non-lapsable pool.  
 
 
III. INDIAN COUNCIL OF MEDICAL RESEARCH  
 
Recommendations/Observations  
 
3.7 The Committee notes that the shortfa ll between the amount allocated and the 
amount projected for ICMR is to the tune  of Rs.630.00 crore which is quite large by 
any standards and is certain to have an adverse bearing on the implementation of 
various research projects of ICMR.  The Committee observes that in view of the 
dynamic international health research envi ronment and the current and future health 
challenges, the role of ICMR is very crucia l and if its projects are plagued with under-
funding, it can have very serious repercu ssions and undermine the desired outcomes 
in the health sector.  The Committee, th erefore, recommends that more funds be 
allocated to ICMR.  Simultaneously, th e Committee impresses upon the ICMR, to 
exercise better fiscal discipline and take cred ible and tangible action to improve the 
financial administration which will ultimatel
y bolster its claims for more funds.                                  
  
 
Action Taken 
 

A request has already been made for a llocation of additional funds to DHR 
including ICMR at the RE stage. ICMR is taking the necessary steps to improve its 
financial administration. Utilisation of funds received by ICMR has been very good.  
 
Recommendations/Observations  
 
3.21 The Committee observes that no single system of health care has the capacity 
to solve all of India’s health care needs. It is in this context that the scientific 
research in the area of traditional medicine assumes added significance. The 
Committee notes that the ICMR is funding 48 projects in traditional medicine. The 
Committee is of the view that it is more important to focus on health outcomes 
rather than health outlays. The Committee, therefore, urges upon the Department 
not to remain complacent by merely fundi ng the 48 projects but to reorient its 
attention for the health outcomes accruing from the above research projects. The 
Committee would like to be apprised of the health outcomes of all the research 
projects under reference. 
 
Action Taken 
 
The observations of the Committee have been noted for compliance. Some of 
the salient health outcomes emerging from the projects under reference are mentioned 
below- 
 
• Successful micro-propagation of Bijasal ( Pterocarpus marsupium Roxb.) , an 
endangered medicinal leguminous tree whose bark is used as a potent anti-
diabetic medicine so that enough wood is available for medicinal purpose and 
the species does not become extinct. 
•  Monograph of medicinal plants having various therapeutic values of Jawa 
Ramgarh area of Rajasthan prepared.   
• 3 medicinal plants ( Ammania baccifera, Annona squamosa and Lycopersicon 
esculentum) showed good antioxidant activity and anti-proliferation activity in 
cancer cell lines. 
• Leaves and testa of Anacardium occidentale (cashew) have been studied for anti-
diabetic activities of their phyto-constituents by various in vitro  and in vivo  
parameters. Catechin, a polyphenol whic h can be used as a nutraceutical has 
been successfully obtained.  
• Fruit of plant Withania coagulus (D oda Paneer) had shown glucose lowering 
effect in animals. 
 
Recommendations/Observations  
 
3.22 The Committee also recomme nds that the task of validation of traditional 
AYUSH drugs and development of new drug s for identified diseases should be 
accomplished within the stipul ated time-frame. Similarly,  the project for validating 
the safety and efficacy of therapeutic practi ce should be completed well in time. It 

would also like to be informed of the ac hievements made so far from the “Golden 
Triangle Partnership, and ICMR’s colla boration with the National Innovation 
Foundation” for validating the safety and efficacy of therapeutic practices. 
 
Action Taken 
 
The recommendations of the Committee have been noted for compliance. The 
actions taken so far under the abovementi oned partnership/collaboration are given 
below – 
 
Golden Triangle Partnership 
 
o Integrated protocols for conducting clin ical trials of seven diseases (Benign 
Prostate Hypertrophy, Osteoporosis, Hypertension, Dyslipidemia, HIV/AIDS, 
Anxiety Neurosis, and Oligospermia) finalised. The clinical trials on 
formulations made available by the Department of AYUSH will be undertaken 
on the basis of these protocols.  
 
ICMR-NIF collaboration 
 
o 5 herbal practices have been selected for the validation. 
o Extramural research projects have been sanctioned on the following topics – 
• Anti-hepatotoxic activity of Abelmoschus esculentus and Datura metel used by 
the herbal healers.  
• Anti diabetic activity of Convolvulus arvensis and Nicotiana tabacum used by 
herbal healers.  
• Evolution of Anti-typhoid activity of Shorea robusta L., an ethno-medicine of 
the Kaatabhai Tribes of Maharashtra. 
 
 
Recommendations/Observations  
 
3.25 The Committee is happy to note that streamlining the process of approval of 
the research proposals is underway. In this era of fast-paced scientific developments, 
speedy approval of the research projects is critical for generating and unleashing full 
potential of scientific knowledge. The Comm ittee, accordingly, recommends that the 
process of approval of the research projects  should be streamlined in such a way that 
their approval is accorded well within the stipulated time frame. 
 
Action Taken 
 
The issue has been addressed. The project review committee meetings are now 
held every 3-4 months. An electronic tracking system has also been developed to fast-
track approvals and for monitoring progress of extramural projects. 
 

V. PROMOTION AND GUIDANCE ON RESEARCH GOVERNANCE ISSUES. 
Recommendations/Observations  
 
5.3 The Committee is dismayed to note that the allocations made for           2008-09 
and 2009-10 have been surrendered in toto due to non-finalization of the programmes.  
The Committee, therefore, feels it imperative for the Department to urgently finalize 
all the projects envisaged under this head so that it can put a strong case for enhanced 
allocation at RE stage.  The Committee woul d also like to be apprised of the progress 
made towards operationalising the above projects. 
Action Taken 
Action on different activities proposed  under Research Governance has been 
initiated to create a National Health Research Forum, map the health research 
institutions and establish a regulatory mechanism and move towards enactment of 
bill.  As discussed above, action on vari ous schemes has  been initiated. After 
pursuing the matter of in-principle approval , revised allocation at RE stage will be 
made as suggested by the Committee.   
 
XII PROVISION FOR PROJECTS/SCHEMES OF NORTH EASTERN AREAS 
AND SIKKIM 
 
Recommendations/Observations  
 
12.5 The Committee notes that the ICMR’s  Regional Medical Research Centre, 
Dibrugarh has been conducting research on various health issues/areas of special 
significance to the North Eastern Region, wh ich have provided significant leads. The 
Committee also notes that during 2009-10, cl ose to 90 studies were continued and 
several new studies have been initiated to address the major health concerns of North 
Eastern Region. The Committee would like to be apprised of the specific health 
products/processes that have been generated  through the research activities/studies 
undertaken in the North Eastern Region and us ed for treatment of ailments specific to 
the people of the region. 
 
Action Taken 
 
The specific health products generated thro ugh the research activities undertaken in 
this region are mentioned below: 
Population Based Cancer Registries:  in the North-East India, were instrumental in 
identifying high incidence of  
(i) Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma in Nagaland  
(ii) Oesophageal Cancer in Assam and  
(iii) Stomach Cancer in Mizoram   
Cardiovascular Diseases:  The Centre established the differential prevalence of 
hypertension in different ethnic groups (A ssamese & Mizo) in tea garden, along with 
salt sensitivity of hypertension. 

Medicinal plants: The Centre identified two local plants possessing good antimalarial 
and mosquito larvicidal properties. 
Mosquito Borne Disease: The Centre developed a module for malaria control in 
forest settings and successfully tested it at the village level.   
Japanese Encephalitis (JE):  The Centre developed an early warning model which is 
able to predict the occurrence of JE cases 2 months in advance at the village level.  
Bancroftian Filariasis:  A module has been developed for the control of bancroftian 
filariasis in tea garden set up. 
Trematode Infections: The Centre has -  
Established the foci of pulmonary paragonimia sis, a disease caused by the lung fluke, 
in NE India.   
Resolved the diagnostic dilemma of p aragonimiasis with that of pulmonary 
tuberculosis in NE region where both the diseases coexist.  
An excretory-secretary antigen based IgG ELISA system was developed for the sero-
diagnosis of human paragon imiasis useful for screen ing human population for 
paragonimiasis in India. 
 

CHAPTER-II 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES 
NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLIES 
 
I. INTRODUCTION 
 
Recommendations/Observations  
 
1.5 The Committee feels that for ensuring t ranslation of research there is a need to 
concentrate on taking research to its logical conclusion in the field of drugs, vaccines 
(both preventive and therapeutic), diagnosis, microbicides, vector and control 
products and platform technologies . The Committee recommends that the 
Department should make all efforts for achieving the above objectives. 
 
Action Taken 
 
As desired by the Committee, the Depart ment is making serious efforts to 
formulate and implement different schemes.  Four schemes covering different work 
allocated to the department have been fo rmulated and have been submitted for in 
principle approval of Planning Commission. 
As recommended by the SCP the action on  the translation of research has been 
taken as a top priority. This programme is  being monitored intensely and adequate 
resources are being provided to achieve the objectives. 
 
III. INDIAN COUNCIL OF MEDICAL RESEARCH 
 
Recommendations/Observations  
 
3.15 The Committee observes that health research projects funded with public 
money should be assessed in terms of tangible health outcomes for the masses and 
there should also be a mechanism for evaluating the health benefits ensuing from such 
research projects. The Committee, therefore, recommends that a system be put in 
place to do audit of heal th research being funded, wholly or partially, with 
government money, so that an assessment could be made as to whether or not the 
health research being done is justified and relevant. 
 
Action Taken 
 
Research audit of ICMR’s intramural pr ojects is being undertaken through a 
three tier system as explained below: - 
A Scientific Advisory Committee (SAC), comp rising subject related experts, assists 
each ICMR Institute/Centre. The SAC over sees the research activities including 
review of ongoing projects and clearing new project. 
A Scientific Advisory Board (SAB) comprising 21 members representing 
different institutions and disciplines, as sp ecified in the Rules and Regulations of the 

ICMR, reviews the reports and recommendations of the Advisory committees/groups 
and offers its advice in regard to the scientific objects of the Council.  
The following are some  additional parameters that are being added to improve the 
quality of the audit - 
• assessment of promising leads; 
• ensuring basic translational research is  being done at the institute level 
so they would assess the feasibility of use by the population of technology 
developed; 
• making technical and financial resources available to achieve this. 
 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
 
3.16 The Committee takes special note of the following achievements of ICMR. 
• A Phase I HIV vaccine trial using the pr ime boost approach was initiated in 
NARI, Pune and TRC, Chennai. The enrolment for the trial has been completed 
and the volunteers are now being followed. 
• Draft guidelines on management of duca l mucous cancer and cervical cancer 
are being finalized on the lines of suggestions of experts. 
• A Web Based Management for Acute Co ronary Events (MACE) Registry 
network has been initiated. 
• New proposal on “ICMR- Indian National  Diabetes Study-Phase I,” has been 
initiated at three states and one Union Territory with the aim to understand 
prevalence of diabetes and pre-diabetes  along its association with the genetic 
aspects. 
 
Action Taken 
 
Needs no comments 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
3.17 The Committee would like to be apprised of the final outcomes of the above 
research projects. 
 
Action Taken 
 
HIV Vaccine Trial: The volunteers enrolled for the study will be followed up till 
December 2010. 
 
Guidelines on Management of bucca l mucosa and cervical cancer: The 
guidelines have been finalised. 

 
Multicentric Management of Acute Coro nary Event Registry project: A Web 
based questionnaire had been designed and is currently being validated by entering 
data from patients registered by MACE registries at different centres. 
 
ICMR-Indian Diabetes Study Phase -1:  The field work is likely to be completed 
by October 2010. The detailed data analysis w ill thereafter be carried out and the final 
outcome is likely to be available in April 2011. 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
3.18 The Committee also notes that a number  of outcomes have been projected for 
the year 2010-11 in respect of ICMR re garding its Regular programme and 
Translational programme, Establishment of new centres, strengthening the 
international cooperation, tribal health in North-East and other under-privileged 
areas/population, manpower developmen t, and health system research. The 
Committee recommends that the desired outc omes should be achieved within the 
fixed time frame. The Committee would also like to be apprised of the achievements 
made in respect of each of the above programmes/projects. 
 
Action Taken 
 
Every effort will be made to achieve the objectives mentioned by the 
Committee. 
The progress achieved so far under the programmes/projects in question is 
mentioned below: 
 
ICMR Project on Cardiovascular Disease Surveillance among the Adivasi 
Population of Wayanad District in Kerala: The project has been completed.  From the 
findings of the project it is clearly evident that underweight is still a major problem 
among the tribal population . The project also evaluated the accuracy of CARDIAC 
CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS BY TELE-AUSCULTAT ION. This preliminary experience 
suggests that transmitted heart sounds have  promise in screening for SHD in remote 
locations. 
 
  RF/RHD registry in Wayanad, Kerala  under Jai Vigyan Mission Mode 
project on ‘Community cont rol of RF/RHD in India’ : The registry has successfully 
completed the laid down objectives of th e study. The highest numbers of RHD cases 
reported by the registry were females in the age group of 30-44 years. The prevalence 
of RHD cases in the registry is 0.47 per 1000 population. Only 1 case of RHD was 
confirmed. The low prevalence of RHD in school children may be due to lower 
diagnostic value of murmur as compared to ECHO in community screening. 
 
Screening for Cancers of Cervix, Breast & Oral Cavity in three districts of 
Himachal Pradesh: ICMR-Government of Himachal P radesh collaborative project on 
Cancer Screening through existing health infrastructure was aimed at screening for 

cancers of cervix, breast and oral cavity, in  three districts of Himachal Pradesh. The 
preparatory phase saw the finalization of strat egy including quality control exercises; 
development of manuals; development of he alth education aids; baseline survey on 
knowledge, attitude and practices related to the chosen cancer sites; establishment of a 
population based cancer registry; purchase  of necessary equipments; preparation of 
proforma and forms; establishment of a referral mechanism; and training of 
professionals and para-professionals. The pr oject was subsequently handed over to 
the state government and intervention  was continued by the State health 
infrastructure using the trained manpower & professional for reporting. The project 
has been extended on request to provide mo re ICMR guidance in execution and data 
analysis. 
 
After review of more than 100 leads/no vel information derived from studies 
carried out at ICMR Institutes/centres, 53 ha ve been identified for translation into 
products / processes / system. Action has been initiated to accomplish the goal of 
Translation. 
 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
3.23 The Committee notes from the Background Material furnished by the 
Department that as many as 16 research projects concerning family planning for 
which a budget of  Rs. 97,53,940/- was committed during 2008-09, are still pending 
and no amount has been released out of the budgeted allocation. In the absence of any 
reasons, the Committee is unable to comp rehend the non-release of the budgeted 
allocation. The Committee therefore, reco mmends that all such research projects 
should be completed at the earliest and bo ttlenecks, if any, should be removed. It 
would also like to be apprised of the reas ons behind the pendency of the projects 
under reference and non-release of the committed funds for those projects. 
 
Action Taken 
 
In order to ensure timely approval of research projects, an electronic tracking 
system has been developed to fast-track approvals and for monitoring progress of 
research projects. The frequency of the project review meetings has also been 
increased and these are being held every 3- 4 months. Due to procedural delays of 
review and approval, the decision about th eir suitability and release of funds was 
delayed. Mechanisms are being put in place to avoid any such delays. A budget of   Rs 
65.29 lakhs was approved in 2009-10 in respect of 4 of the 16 proposals mentioned 
above that were finally approved after the prescribed peer review. 
 
 
IV. PROMOTION, COORDINATION AND DEVELOPMENT OF BASIC, 
APPLIED AND CLINICAL RESEARCH  
 
Recommendations/Observations 

 
4.1 Plan allocation for Promotion, Coor dination, and Develo pment of Basic, 
Applied and Clinical research was Rs.50.00 Crore for 2008-09.  However, the schemes 
could not be finalized and therefore no expenditure was incurred under this head 
during 2008-09.  These schemes could not be commenced during          2009-10 as well, 
as a result of which Rs.2.00 crore allocated under this head remained unspent. Rs. 
49.00 crore has been allocated for the pu rpose for 2010-11.  The Department has 
informed the Committee that this will be its major activity for which it had proposed 
an amount of Rs.369.00 crores for 2010-11.  Th e enhanced level of projected demands 
was meant for commencements of the following 5 new sub-schemes:-  
• Special support to the Medical Colleges for medical research 
• Establishment of Model Rural Health Research Units 
• Establishment of a Network of Virus Diagnostic Laboratories 
• Programme for gender and health Programme for online teaching and learning 
 
Action Taken 
 
The schemes have been sent for in-principle approval to Planning Commission. 
 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
4.2 The project proposals are likely to be finalized within the next three months, 
after which they would be moved for mandatory clearances.  The Department has 
further informed that Rs.49.00 crore may no t be sufficient to commence the above 
schemes and therefore it proposes to commence the smaller programmes, i.e. 
Programme for Gender and Health and Prog ramme for on-line teaching and learning 
on medical research and will seek a revision at the RE stage to take up all the five 
programmes. 
 
Action Taken 
 
The schemes have been sent for in principle approval to the Planning 
Commission. 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
4.3 The Committee notes that the above sch emes were targeted to be commenced 
during 2008-09.  However they could not be  finalized even during 2009-10.  Three 
years of the Eleventh Plan have elapse d and the inordinate delay witnessed in 
finalization of these ambitious schemes le aves the Committee wondering as to how 
the envisaged objectives under the schemes would be achieved in the next two years 
of the Plan.  Since the Department has not shed any light on the factors responsible for 
the inordinate delay, the Committee can only  guess that these schemes got stuck in 
the quagmire of approval delays arising out of bureaucratic red-tape, leading to scare 

resources remaining idle during 2008-09 and 2009-10, which could otherwise have 
been put to more productive us.  However, the Committee is of the considered view 
that lack of funding should not be allowed  to come in the way of commencement of 
the above five sub-schemes.  The Committee notes that due to reduced allocation, the 
Department would not be able to start majo r activities under this head like Special 
support to Medical Colleges for medical research, Establishm ent of Model Rural 
Health Research Units, and Establishmen t of a Network of Virus Diagnostic 
Laboratories.  The Committee, therefore, lends its full support for enhanced allocation 
for the above sub-schemes and recommends that adequate funds be allocated for 
satisfactory operationalization of the 5 schemes mentioned above.  The Committee 
simultaneously exhorts the Department to obtain mandatory clearances without 
further loss of time.  
 
Action Taken 
 
The Department has prepared schemes to  implement all the new activities 
proposed (which are listed in 4.1).  The planning of the schemes began in the 
beginning of 2009 (2008-09) when new Secretary joined and these ideas started getting 
debated in PM SAC, Cabinet SAC, differe nt Expert Groups constituted for the 
purpose.  These were presented to the Planning Commission during the mid-term 
review and now have been developed into  schemes. These are being submitted to 
Planning Commission for its in principle appr oval so that the implementation should 
begin within 2010-11.  The Department will tr y to convince the Planning Commission 
to allocate sufficient funds and will strive to obtain mandatory clearances. 
 
VIII. INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION IN MEDICAL AND HEALTH 
RESEARCH  
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
8.4 The Committee regrets to note that this is yet another case of poor planning 
and unrealistic projections for allocation of funds, leading not only to substantial 
under-utilization of funds but also to th e above programmes remaining non-starter.

organizations/agencies concerned to implem ent the projects envisaged under this 
head in time-bound manner.

Scheme has been sent to Planning Commission for in principle approval.

 The Committee is constrained to note  that the Department’s reply lacks 
clarity and totality.  For example, the Department’s reply is silent about 
institutionalizing the Coordination mechanism, as recommended by the 
Committee.  Similarly, the Department had earlier informed the Committee that an 
Implementation Committee to develop the Gu idelines for coordination with other 
agencies/organizations was on the jo b and the Committee had sought to be 
apprised of the progress made in that regard.  The Committee had also 
recommended to draw up an action plan to implement the projects under this head 
in a time-bound manner.   
 
The Committee is not satisfied that the Department has attempted to respond 
to its recommendations by merely stating th at “Scheme has been sent to Planning 
Commission for in-principle approval” with out shedding any light on the other 
two issues.  The Committee, therefore, ur ges upon the Department to exercise 
greater care and circumspection while furnishing action taken report in future.  
 
 

XI. MATTERS RELATING TO SC IENTIFIC SOCIETIES AND 
ASSOCIATIONS, CHARITABLE AND RELIGIOUS ENDOWNMENTS IN 
MEDICINE AND HEALTH RESEARCH AREAS. 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
11.3 The Committee deprecates the Departme nt for its inability to implement one 
project after another on time and projecti ng budgetary demands in an unrealistic 
manner. This calls for serious introspectio n. The Committee genuinely hopes that the 
project envisaged under this head should  commence during the current fiscal and 
exhorts the Department with all the power at its command to start the ground work 
for implementation of the programmes under this head in right earnest. 
 
Action Taken 
 
The scheme has been sent to Planning Commission for in principle approval. 
 
Comments of the Committee 
 
The Committee would urge upon the Depa rtment to pursue the approval of 
the project with Planning Commission so that time-over run and the resultant cost 
escalation do not plague the scheme.  
  
XIII. HPV VACCINE 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
13.2     Taking serious view of procedural and ethical lapses on the part of the 
Ministry, the Committee sought the matter of a llowing trial of the vaccine as also the 
approval for its marketing in the countr y to be enquired into by a premier 
investigating agency and to take further a ppropriate follow-up action in the matter. It 
also asked that findings of the investigatin g agency and the follow-up action taken in 
this regard may be furnished to the Committee at the earliest. The Committee taking a 
serious view in the matter recommends to th e Department of Health Research that in 
future all guidelines and norms should be ad hered to before allowing trials of any 
drug including vaccines on Indian popula tion. The Committee also recommends that 
the Drug Controller General of India should observe optimum precautions and follow 
all norms and guidelines while allowing marketing of any drug including the vaccines 
in the Indian market. 
 
Action Taken 
 
PATH in partnership with  State Governments of Gu jarat and Andhra Pradesh 
was implementing an operational research study related to cancer of the cervix 
prevention in India.  ICMR is providing technical support & consultation for 
development of protocol and plan of monitoring.  

 
The study utilized both the brands of HPV vaccine available in the market (Gardasil 
by Merck in Andhra Pradesh; and Cervirix by GSK in Gujarat).  
 
In view of certain complaints receiv ed, the State Governments have been 
advised not to carry out further vaccination till further orders.  To ascertain the facts 
of the matter, Hon’ble Minister for Health  & Family Welfare appointed a Committee 
comprising of Dr. S.S. Agarwal, former Director, Advanced Centre for Training, 
Research, Education on Cancer, Dr. S.P. Aggarwal, former DGHS and Dr. Sunita 
Mittal, HoD, Obstetrics & Gynaecology, AIIMS to investigate ethical issues raised in 
this matter.  
 
Comments of the Committee 
 
 The Committee observes that as a re sult of its intervention, the State 
Governments have been advised by the Department not to carry out HPV 
vaccination and a Committee has been appointed to investigate ethical issues raised 
in the matter. The Committee is not aware about the date of setting up of the 
Committee.  However, absence of any specific time-line for submission of Report of 
the Committee in the Action Taken Note given by the Department makes the 
Committee somewhat apprehensive.  Like so many Committees set up by the 
Government, findings of this Committee, as and when received, may remain on 
paper only.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that every effort should be 
made to expedite the Report of this Co mmittee so that real facts about the HPV 
Vaccine trial are made known without any further delay and corrective measures 
not only in respect of this case but for a ll such ongoing/proposed clinical trials of 
drugs/vaccines are taken.  The Committee also recommends that the Department 
should at least now work in clos e coordination with other concerned 
departments/organizations to undertake a comprehensive analysis of the process of 
granting permission to research studies having hazardous effects on health and put 
in place a fool-proof system for pre-empting unethical research studies.  
 
 
 
XIV MANPOWER REQUIREMENTS FOR DHR AND ICMR 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
14.8       The Committee is surprised to note  that our premier Institute in the field of 
medical research has been working with th e minimum staff for all these years. The 
very fact that not a single post has been  created during the last 25 years confirms 
Committee’s concerns in this regard. Not only this, a large number of  posts, that too, 
in scientific and technical grade are lying vacant. The Committee is not aware since 
when such a situation has been continuing . The Committee can imagine the kind of 
work stress being faced by our scientists, specially during the time of epidemic 
outbreaks. The Committee recommends that al l the existing vacant posts in ICMR 

should be filled up without any further delay. All 500 posts of scientists and 1000 
matching posts of research fellows and technical posts should be created at the earliest 
and filled up. This exercise needs to be c arried out in a time-bound manner. It should 
be ensured that unduly long time is not taken in getting the posts created, followed by 
a protracted exercise of getting them filled up. Similarly, concerted efforts would also 
be required for creation and filling up of 210 posts of scientists and 400 posts of 
technical staff required for the Department  of Health Research. The Department will 
have to play a proactive role so that lack of specialized manpower does not hamper 
the crucial research activities, both ongoing and proposed. 
 
Action Taken 
  
 Needs no comments. 
 
Comments of the Committee 
 
 The Committee had invested the creation of posts of scientists and matching 
posts of research fellows and technical po sts with Parliamentary support and it was 
the obligation of the Department to make earnest efforts to apprise the authorities 
concerned of the Committee’s recommendation in this regard so that necessary 
action could be initiated towards creating and filling up the posts.

“needs no comments”.  The phrase employed by the Department lends credence to 
the impression that it does not attach much  importance to the creation of necessary 
posts.  The Committee, therefore, urges upon the Department to attend to the 
matter with an astute sense of sincerity and urgency.

achievement of the physical targets, which are on the lower side in respect of several 
important components of the Programme. The response of the Department in no 
way addresses the issues raised by the Committee. In the absence of any 
justification, the Committee, as it said ear lier, can only infer that some serious 
problem areas in planning and the subsequent execution strategies of most of the 
components of the Programme exist. The De partment needs to take up this aspect 
very seriously. 
IV  SETTING UP OF NEW BLOOD COMPONENT SEPARATION UNITS 
(BCSUs) 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
 
4.2 The Committee is constrained to observ e that the data made available to the 
Committee through the response to a query made twice reveals that the Department 
has fixed a target of 162 for setting up of new Blood Component Separation Units by 
the end of the Eleventh Plan . The Committee notes that no  target was fixed for the 
first year, i.e., 2007 – 08, and for 2008 – 09 an d 2009 – 10, 40 BCSUs each were kept as 
targets. However, a cumulative achievemen t of only 47 BCSUs could be made till 
February 2010. Out of the total target of 162 un its for the Eleventh Plan period, a total 
of 115 more such units are required to be set up during the last two years of the 
Eleventh Plan period. The Committee would like the same to be clarified. 
 
 
Action Taken 
 
 
It is submitted that under Phase – III of National AIDS Control Programme, the 
target for setting up of 80 Blood Componen t Separation Units was fixed. As per the 

procurement cycle, the procurement of equipm ents for these units was to be taken up 
during 2008 – 09 and 2009 – 10 for 40 set of equi pments during each year.  No target 
was fixed during the 1st year, in view of the regulatory requirement for physical 
infrastructure for setting up of BCSUs, wh ich entails 7 rooms with the total covered 
area of 150 sq. metres and necessary electrical and mechanical fittings. 
It is also submitted that even after the procurement of equipments, the process 
of obtaining a license from the Drugs Controlle r General (India) is at various stages of 
processing viz. preliminary inspection; joint inspection and final inspection etc. which 
was followed up with the concerned authorities at every stage. Because of this, out of 
the 80 such units, 49 units have obtained a license to operate and for the remaining 
units, the matter is being followed up. 
Thus, the target for setting up of BCSUs as reflected in the report as 162, is the 
cumulative target for NACP, Phase – III.  
 
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE 
 
 The Committee has been informed that under Phase III of NACO, against the 
target during 2007-08 to 2009-10 for setting up of 80 Blood Component Separation 
Units, 40 Units have obtained a license to  operate so far. The Committee is not 
aware whether the required infrastructure of 7 fully equipped rooms with total 
covered area of 150 sq. meters has been made available for these units. For the 
remaining 31 units, the process of procuring a license from the Drug Controller 
General of India is yet to be completed. Against this backdrop, the Committee is 
not very hopeful about the achievement level of 162 Blood Component Separation 

Units to be set up under Phase III of NA CO. The Committee can only emphasize 
that every conceivable effort needs to be made to accomplish this target. 
 
V.  SETTING UP OF NEW DISTRICT LEVEL BLOOD BANKS. 
 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
 
5.3 The Committee is dismayed at the fact that the Department has not been able to 
take up the matter of setting up of the di strict level blood banks with a sense of 
urgency. The Department itself is aware  that these 39 Blood Banks have been 
identified on the basis of an assessment of  urgent requirement in underserved areas. 
Hence, a delay in setting up of the blood ba nks as envisaged, is against Department’s 
obligations to see that the facilities reach these underserved areas. Most of the reasons 
cited for the delay are non-availability of  adequate infrastructure, manpower and 
delay in issuance of license. The Department needs to play a pro-active role by taking 
up the matter with the concerned State Gove rnments as well as the agencies at an 
appropriate level to expedite the procedural  formalities. The Department should also 
consider providing appropriate additional funds, if required, for infrastructure and 
manpower related matters so that there is no delay due to financial constraints. 
 
Action Taken 
 
It is submitted that the target of taki ng up blood banks in the 39 districts was 
identified during the planning of National AIDS Control Programme (NACP), Phase – 
III; wherein both National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) and concerned State 
Governments have specific roles. NACO was supposed to provide equipment and the 
annual recurring grant for one Lab Techni cian and consumables, while the State 
Government has to provide physical infrastr ucture in terms of building with a space 

of 100 sq. mts in 5(five) rooms; manpower  in terms of Medical Officer, Laboratory 
Technician, Nurse and support staff. As pe r the laid down scheme for modernization 
of blood banks, the funds for infrastructu re and manpower are not included in the 
Pattern of Assistance and is the responsibility of the State Government. 
 
NACO has already completed the procurement of equipments and the matter 
is followed up with concerned State Gove rnments, so that once the physical 
infrastructure in terms of building is ready, further action can be initiated. 
 
In view of this follow up, Blood Banks in 8 ou t of the 39 identified districts have come 
up now and for the remaining blood banks, continuous follow up is in process. 
 
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE 
 
 The Committee acknowledges the stand of the Department that the funds for 
infrastructure and manpower are not included in the Pattern of Assistance and is 
the responsibility of the State Governme nts. Factual position as given by the 
Department clearly indicates that majority  of the State Governments have failed to 
fulfil their commitment of providing physica l infrastructure, i.e. a building having 
an area of 100 sq.mts. and required manpower of Medical Officer, Lab Technician, 
Nurse and Support Staff. Moreover, when NACO has already procured the 
equipments for these Blood Banks, they  need to be supplemented by State 
Governments coming forward with fulfillment of their commitments. The 
Committee can only reiterate that the Depart ment has to play a pro-active role by 
taking up the matter with the concerned State Governments, if need be at the 
highest level. It can also help the States financially which are facing resource 

constraints. The Committee is of the firm op inion that the Department has to play 
the role of catalyst in achieving the targets under this component rather than 
remaining rigid on procedural aspects. 
  
Recommendations/Observations 
 
5.7 The Committee welcomes this new initiative  of the Department for establishing 
four Metro Blood Banks as Centres of Excellence. However, the Committee is 
unhappy to note that the slow progress of th e Department in realizing this initiative 
which has been pending since 2008 – 09. Th ese blood banks would not only act as 
model blood banks with latest equipments and technology but would also be of great 
help in meeting the ever rising dema nds of these metro cities. The Committee 
however notes that from the records available with it, that no dead lines have been set 
regarding making the same functional. Keep ing in mind the delay already made in 
implementation of this initiative, the Co mmittee recommends to the Department to 
have a targeted approach in making the four metro blood banks functional at the 
earliest. The Committee would also like to draw the attention of the Department to the 
undue delay in the operationalisation of mode l Blood Bank at Tirupati.  Infrastructure 
for the Blood Bank has already been provided by the State Government. The Secretary 
assured the Committee that action for se nding the equipment for the Blood Bank 
would be taken immediately. 
  
Action Taken 
 
It is submitted that a road-map has been prepared for setting up of Metro 
Blood Banks in Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai an d Kolkata following the approval of the 
Cabinet. The requisite land has been made  available by the State Governments of 

West Bengal and Tamil Nadu, while the issue of allotment of land is followed up with 
the State Government of Maharashtra.  
The Design DPR Consultants for prepara tion of Architectural Drawings are 
already in place. The Preliminary Drawings  have already been approved for three 
Metro Blood Bank sites at Kolkata, Chennai and Delhi.  
It is submitted that the construction wo rk for these sites is expected to start 
during the current Financial Year itself. 
In regard to the Model Blood Bank in Tirupati, it is submitted that the proto-
type of equipments to be supplied to this blood bank has already been approved by 
an Expert Committee appointed by NACO. The equipments for the blood bank will be 
supplied and installed during the month of August 2010. 
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE 
 
The Committee observes that the establ ishment of four Metro Blood Banks 
as Centres of Excellence aimed at having four model Blood Banks in Delhi, 
Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata with latest equipments and technology is in its 
third year of conceptualisation but still a lot needs to be done to actually realize the 
same.  Though the Department hopes to start construction on the three sites, the 
issue of land in case of Mumbai is st ill being sorted out. The Committee would 
like to emphasize that the road-map prepared for setting up these Blood Banks 
needs to be adhered to by all concerned, especially the State Implementing 
Agencies. The Committee is not aware abou t the targeted date of completion of 
construction work for these Blood Banks  which is expected to start during the 
current financial year. One must also not fo rget the fact that these Blood Banks can 

be considered fully functional only wh en they are well-equipped having the 
required infrastructure and manpower. As regards the Model Blood Bank in 
Tirupati, the Committee hopes that by no w it would have started functioning as 
per the latest information submitted by the Department. 
VIII  ART CENTERS 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
8.3 The Committee is satisfied that at pres ent the number of patients undergoing 
second line of ART is within the manageab le range. However, the Committee is of the 
considered opinion that the number of cent res of excellence being limited to just 10 
where the patients can have treatment fac ilities, the patients, especially the poor 
people residing far away from theses cent res, will have to spend a lot of money for 
transportation for visiting these centres regularly.  The Committee thinks that with the 
facilities of ART centres expanding, more nu mber of patients requiring second line of 
treatment is going to increase considerably.  Accordingly, the Committee recommends 
to the Department to have a realistic assess ment of the requirement of new Centres of 
Excellence with a view to make the facilitie s for treatment available within reasonable 
distance of the patients. 
Action Taken 
An assessment on the distribution of pa tients referred as “treatment failures” 
and those who were put on 2nd line ART is being done.  Subsequently, ART centres 
will be identified based on volume of eligible cases and capacity to provide 2nd line 
ART.  During 2010-11,  8-10 ART centres will be upgraded through training, provision 

of 2nd line drugs and linkage with viral load  testing facilities.  More centres will be 
upgraded based on volume of patients on 2nd line ART.   
  
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE 
 
The Committee appreciates that the Department is undertaking an 
assessment about the distribution of patient s referred as “treatment failures” and 
those who were put on 2nd line ART.  The Committee would like to have the 
details of such assessment as well as of  those ART centres wh ich will be upgraded 
through training, provision of 2nd line drugs and linkage with viral load testing 
facilities during  2010-11. 
IX  NEW INITIATIVES 
Recommendations/Observations 
9.2 The Committee is pained at the slow progress in establishing the National 
Blood Transfusion Authority and setting up of a Plasma Fractionation Plant. Both 
these initiatives are very important. It is very disappointing that the same still remains 
on paper even after two years. The Commi ttee would like to be informed about the 
reasons for the inordinate delay and the de adline by which the same would be set up. 
It recommends to the Department to make  all conceivable efforts to achieve the 
aforesaid targets at the earliest. 
Action Taken 
 
It is submitted that after approval of  the Cabinet, an Expert Committee was 
constituted to finalise adoption of techno logy for this project in view of the highly 
complex technical nature of the project.  The Expert Group has recommended for 
adoption of “Cohn n Chromatography Techno logy” for this project. Subsequently, an 
Expression of Interest was invited from  interested firms to work as Project 

Management Consultant. The process of sele ction of Project Management Consultant 
is in progress. 
In regard to setting up of National Bl ood Transfusion Author ity, the approval 
of Cabinet is under process. The National Blood Transfusion Authority will be set up, 
after approval of the Cabinet on this initiative. 
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE 
 
The Committee is dismayed at the manner in which establishment of the 
National Blood Transfusion Authority and setting up of a Plasma Fractionation 
Plant is still entangled in paper work. As  both these components are crucial for 
furthering the objectives of NACO, th e Committee had called for reasons for the 
inordinate delay and the deadline by wh ich these two would be set up. Though 
the reply of the Department briefly indicates the progress made so far, nowhere it 
has specified the reasons for the delay or the timelines set by it. In the opinion of 
the Committee this is a case of poor plan ning and implementation strategy on the 
part of the Department. The Committee re commends to the Department to revisit 
its strategy and set out necessary correctiv e measures to achieve these two targets 
at the earliest. 
XII NATIONAL PEDIATRIC INITIATIVE 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
 
12.3 The Committee is very concerned at th e increasing number  of HIV+ children 
and rising trend of HIV prevalence in  pregnant women in low prevalence / 
vulnerable States of North India. However, the Committee considers it to be due to 
Department’s proactive approach in identify ing and tracking the HIV+ mothers or it 

m a y  b e  a n  i n d i c a t i o n  o f  r i s e  o f  t h e  d isease in the low prevalence States.  The 
Committee would recommend to the Department to keep a strict vigil on rising trends 
of HIV prevalence among pregnant wome n in low prevalence States and take 
immediate steps to contain the same.  The Committee may be informed of the specific 
steps taken by the Department in this regard. 
 
12.4 The Committee is pained to imagine the plight of the small children who 
would be requiring the ART treatment in the long run.  The Committee recommends 
to the Department to intensify its approach  to detect the HIV+ children by targeting 
the HIV+ mothers and ensuring full care and support to them.  The Committee may 
be informed about the status of all HIV+ children in India, state-wise. 
  
Action Taken 
 
A  two prong strategy is being implemented to check number of HIV+ children:- 
a) Scale-up identification of HIV+ pregnant women by offering HIV counselling and 
testing routinely at Antenatal Clinics. These identified as HIV+ will be assessed 
for eligibility of ART by performing CD4 count.  This would require better linkage 
between ICTC and ART centres.  Thos e not eligible for ART will be given 
prophylactic treatment.   
b) Follow-up of children exposed to HI V (children born to  HIV+ mother and 
children getting breast feeding from HIV+  mother). They will be identified and 
tested for HIV through latest techno logy (DNA-PCR) for early diagnosis and 
treatment. Active screening of vulnerable children by involving NGOs and 
outreach workers has been initiated. 
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE
 

 
  The Committee had called for a status of all HIV+ children in India, State-
wise and had specifically recommended to the Department to keep a strict vigil on 
rising trends of HIV prevalence among pregnant women in low prevalence States 
and, accordingly, had sought details of th e specific steps taken by the Department 
in this regard.  The Department in its response has just reproduced the existing 
procedure being adopted by it. The specif ic information sought by the Committee 
is missing. The Department may, accordingly, provide necessary details in this 
regard.

All India Institute of Ayurveda, New Delhi 
Recommendations/Observations  
4.1.4 The Committee is happy to note the submission  of the Department that there is no change in the e stimates of the project

May 2010. However, more than two years have already elapsed since the Cabinet approved the project in January, 2008 but the 
designs and plan of construction of the project are  yet to be approved by the Delhi Development Author ity (DDA). Therefore, 
the construction of the building scheduled to commence in 2009-10 itself has been rescheduled for May, 2010.

 The Delhi Fire Service, Airport Authority of India , Delhi Urban Art Commission and Delhi Pollution Control Committee

drawings of the building with the DDA at the highes t level. The Committee also recommends that the pro gress of the 
construction of the building be monitored at a suff iciently higher level in the Department so that no room is left for time

against the sanctioned strength (pre-upgradation fr om 25 bed to 50 bedded Hospital) of 9 Doctors/ Spec ialists, 6 have been 
posted in the Hospital. 

 Action for filling up the vacancies of Medical Off icer (AY) on ‘direct recruitment’ basis through UPS C will be initiated

North-Eastern Institute of Ayurveda and Homoeopathy, Shillong 
Recommendations/Observations  
5.5.4 The Committee views with serious concern the tardy progress made in the operationalisation of a national level Institute of 
AYUSH system of health-care in the much-needed N-E region of the country. The Committee would like to point out that the 
total cost of the first phase of the project is est imated at Rs.67.50 crore. The Committee wonders as to how far the Task Force 
headed by the Secretary (AYUSH) constituted for imp lementation of the project would prove to be helpfu l. The Committee 
does not have much hope even in the first phase of the project taking off by the end of Eleventh Plan. With reported expenditure 
of only Rs. 9.00 crore upto 2009-10 and proposed pr ovision of Rs.17.00 crore for 2010-11, one can draw  the very obvious 
conclusion. The Committee apprehends that chances o f there being both time-overruns and cost-overruns are very much there. 
The Committee can only emphasize that the Task Force has to vigorously supervise the implementation of first phase of NEIAH 
at Shillong, identifying the problem areas along with simultaneously moving for removal of the same. Only then, this ambitious 
project would succeed in becoming functional in the real sense. 
Action Taken  
 Implementation of the project picked up with vigor ous follow up of the matter with the Project Management Consultants, 
M/s HSCC (India) Limited. The contractor for constr uction of the building has been appointed and the c ontractor has already 
moved his manpower and machinery to the constructio n site for commencement of the construction. Constr uction of the 
building has commenced in October, 2010. 
 In the meantime, the Director of the Institute has  been appointed with effect from 2.6.2010. He has s tarted functioning 
from Shillong. The project is expected to complete well in time. As regards the apprehension of the Committee about utilization 
of funds, it is submitted that actual expenditure would increase with the pace of construction. 
 

North Eastern Institute of Folk Medicine, Passighat, Arunachal Pradesh 
Recommendations/Observations  
5.6.2  Eleventh Plan outlay for the Institute was R s.41.00 crore. Although Rs.16.69 crore were allocat ed during the first three 
years of the Plan period, Institute continues to be  at a proposal stage. As a result allocated funds r emained unutilized. While 
trying to assess the different stages of preparatory exercise for starting the Institute, the Committee is surprised to note that after 
the Cabinet approval in February, 2008, it took ful l one year (2008-09) for appointing the Project Con sultant, i.e. , M/s HSCC 
and getting the required land. However, both the actions had to undergo a drastic change. M/s HLL took the place of M/s HSCC 
as Project Consultant. Issue of allotment of disputed land ultimately got the necessary clearance from the concerned authorities. 
As a result, another year passed with the project continuing to be at the proposal stage. The Committee is constrained to observe 
that due care was not taken in both the selection o f Project Consultant and selection of Project site by all the concerned 
agencies. The Committee apprehends that the initial  estimated cost of Rs.32.88 crore for the Project w ould undoubtedly 
undergo a drastic enhancement. 
Action Taken  
 The project of the North Eastern Institute of Folk  Medicine, Passighat was got delayed a little due t o delay in transfer of 
the forest land by the State Govt. The State Forest  Department kept the transfer of land pending due t o non-payment of the 
diversion cost of the land by the State Health Depa rtment. As per the agreement, the cost of the land is to be borne by the State 
Govt. However, in order to expedite transfer of lan d, the environmental impact study of the land was d one and drawings and 
designs of the building taken up by the Project Management Consultants, M/s HLL Lifecare Limited. Now, the prbj6ct is in full 
swing. Tenders have been issued and contractor has been finalized. The actual work commenced from August, 2010. 
 After careful planning and tactful handling of the  project at senior level and continuous monitoring, it has been possible to 
keep the project cost within the limit of the initi al cost. Hence, it is expected that there will be n o cost escalation in the project 
cost. 
Recommendations/Observations  
5.6.3  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the remaining approvals and pre-construction activities may be expedited so 
that construction of the building is started within the first half of 201 0-11. For this, the Project Monitoring Committee will have 
to be constantly on alert. The Committee desires to  be apprised of the necessary steps taken and the m odalities worked out to 
ensure completion of the project on time and also check cost overruns of the project. (Para 5.6.3) 
Action Taken  
 The Project Monitoring Committee headed by Secreta ry (AYUSH) is constantly monitoring the project. The Government 
has appointed a senior IAS Officer, belonging to the region, as Director of the Institution. It would help better coordination with 
the local administration and State Government authorities.

Recommendations/Observations

for upgrading functions and facilities of reputed i nstitutions to the levels of excellence. The Commit tee, however, finds that 
very few reputed institutions have been covered under the Scheme so far, majority of them not being well-known institutions of

 At present, there are 27 institutions/organization s/NGOs which have been receiving funds under the Sc heme. These are 
reputed institutions in the field of AYUSH. The selection of these institutions/organizations/NGOs has been made strictly on the

 For monitoring purposes also, the Department has s et up different monitoring committees for each proposal consisting of

2.1.7  The Committee is not happy to note that the plan allocation had to be reduced at RE stage in so me of the most important

fully convinced with the reasons cited by the Department for reduction of allocation at RE Stage as due to inadequate allocation

get necessary approvals from local authorities, it is a sad commentary on its functioning and calls in to question its 
seriousness of exercising fiscal prudence. Now that all the groundwork has been completed, the Committee would expect 
the Department to monitor the progress in respect o f all items of work meticulously and come up with s ubstantive

Setting up of National Board for Medicinal Plants

coordinating all matters relating to medicinal plan ts and support policies and programmes for growth o f trade, export, 

conservation and cultivation of medicinal plants. D espite the above fact, only Rs. 40.00 crore could b e made available

was Rs. 39.19 crore as on 15th March, 2010, the Com mittee is pretty certain that the entire allocation  under this head 
must have been utilized by the end of the financial  year 2009-10. The Committee observes that while th ere have been 
recurrent savings under some of the heads with the budgeted amount being surrended year after year, su ch an 
important initiative as setting up of NMPB had to s uffer financial crunch due to skewed priorities of the Department. 
The Committee would, therefore, tend to infer that there was something wrong with prioritizing policy of Department of 
AYUSH and impress upon it to be more careful in this regard.  
CGHS Ayurveda Hospital and Educational Institutions

3.2 The Committee has been observing that setting u p of the Pharmacy Council has been getting unduly d elayed. There is no 
standardized and uniform education system or curriculum available for training pharmacists in AYUSH. To facilitate regulation 
of education and practice of pharmacists in this se ctor, the Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy Pharmacy Council Bill, 2005 
was introduced in Parliament on 12th August, 2005. The Committee submitted its Report on the Bill to t he Parliament on 28th 
July, 2006. The Committee finds it very disturbing that inspite of it submitting its Report well in ti me, the revised Bill is yet to 
come before Parliament. Mere allocation of funds ye ar after year will not result in setting up of the long-awaited Pharmacy 
Council of Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy. 
Recommendations/Observations  
3.3 The Committee does not have much hope about the  proposed Council coming up during the Eleventh Pla n period. 
Committee’s apprehensions arise from the allocation  of Rs. 1 lakh projected by the Department for 2010 -11 which has been

VI.  RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT 
Recommendations/Observations  
6.6 Committee’s attention has been drawn by some re ports about successful treatment of Cancer patients by Ayurvedic drugs. 
On a specific query about the veracity of these rep orts, the Committee was pleasantly surprised to not e the significant 
achievements made by the Ayurvedic practitioners as indicated below:- 
- On the recommendation of the Scientific Advisory Committee (Ayurveda), the CCRAS has initiated the s tudy of 
‘CARCTOL’ a proprietary medicine of Vaid Nand Lal Tiwari of Jaipur supposed to have anti-cancer properties. For 
verifying the therapeutic claim, standardization work has been completed by the Council. Safety and toxicity studies 
have also been completed. As informed by the Ex. Director-General, CCRAS, ‘CARCTOL’ has also been subjected 
to in-vitro study at Advanced Cancer Research Centr e of TATA, Mumbai against 14 types of human cancer cells 
out of which it was found effective against pancrea tic and lung cancer. It was placed on record that C ARCTOL is 
being used for treatment of cancer: patients both i n the country and abroad. After preparation of doss iers, multi-
centric clinical trials will be conducted. 
-  Pre-clinical study of ‘Cancer Gaza Kesari’ a pro prietary drug of Vaid Krishan Gopal of Ajmer has al so been 
conducted by the Council in collaboration with Vete rinary College, Chennai. The study revealed that th e drug 
significantly reduced the mammary tumor incidence, latency, frequency, rate of growth and malignancy. It was also 
subjected to in-vitro study against 14 types of hum an cancer cell line, out of which it has shown to b e of effect 
against Pancreatic and Lung Cancer. 
-  Pilot project was sanctioned by the Ministry in 1996 to study the effects of metal based formulatio ns prepared by 
Vaid Balendu Prakash of Dehradun in the treatment of Acute pro-myllolic Leukemia. The Committee was informed 
that the drug was patented jointly by the Council w ith Germany. The Committee was also given to unders tand the 
Vaid Balendu Prakash has been treating Cancer patie nts with the drug. On a specific qucry it was clari fied that the 
Indo-German patent was a process patent. So far onl y a pilot study of 21 patients has been conducted b y the 
Council. Multi- Cultural Clinical Trials of the drug were to be undertaken which would take four years. 
-  The Committee also notes that ethical approval a nd release of funds for clinical trial of AYUSH QOL-2C at AIIMS 
has been completed. Registration of patent is to be initiated shortly. Simultaneously, 10 patients have been enrolled 
for study at St. Johns Medical College, Bangalore. This drug is reported to improve quality of life of those receiving 
chemotherapy /radiotherapy. 
Action Taken  
 The encouraging observations of the august committ ee have been noted.  

Recommendations/Observations  
6.7 The Committee places on record its appreciation  of commendable work being done by the Research Cou ncils on their 
own and also in collaboration with well-known institutions in the country and abroad. Work of the CCRAS touches both routine 
ailments as well as chronic ailments where permanen t cure is yet to be found inspite of giant strides made by the modern 
medical sciences. In such a scenario, for the treat ment of the most deadly cancer disease, any signifi cant achievement by any 
system of medicine should be welcome to all. The ‘C ommittee considers it a strange irony that although  large number of 
patients are getting relief by the drugs formulated by individuals after years of their single-handed research, official recognition 
still remains elusive to them. The Committee strong ly advocates the streamlining and expediting of the  official certification 
process, so that humanity at large gets the long-awaited relief. 
Action Taken  
 Whenever any claim is submitted to Council, the sa me are examined and put before Scientific Advisory Committee to 
carry out scientific validation. In this context, t wo claims on cancer have been subjected to Pre-clin ical Studies based on which 
clinical trial will be carried out as per lead. If any drug is finally marketed, the benefit will be s hared by Council and the 
claimant. But there is no provision of Certification by the Council. 
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE  
 The Committee is not satisfied with the evasive re ply given by the Department. Keeping in view that t here is no 
effective cure/treatment for cancer in the modern s ystem of medicines, the Department should make all out efforts to 
exploit any significant achievement by any system o f medicine towards treatment/cure of such a deadly disease. The 
adequate and effective mechanism should be in place  to expedite scientific validation of any claim in this regard. The 
Committee notes with dismay that the Department has  failed so far in carrying out-scientific validatio n of such claims 
due to procedural delays and lack of adequate resea rch work and expertise in this regard. The Committe e would 
reiterate once again that the process of clinical t rial on two claims of cancer needs to start at the earliest. Contention of 
the Department that in the event of any drug being finally marketed, the benefit would be shared by the Council and the 
claimant, does not lead to the ultimate goal of pro viding relief to patients suffering from cancer. It  is a well-known fact 
that this disease is spreading at an alarming rate with new dimensions emerging. In such a scenario, t he Department 
along with the Research Council needs to play a pro-active role.

Recommendations/Observations  
9.1 The AYUSH system of medicine is governed by Dru gs & Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Rules made thereunder. Enforcement 
provision of Chapter IV A of Drugs & Cosmetics Act,  1940 is the responsibility of State Governments. E stablishment of State 
Drug Testing Laboratories is also a statutory responsibility of States under the Act. To provide financial assistance to States for 
strengthening enforcement mechanism, the Drug Quali ty Control Scheme was started in IXth plan. Over th e years, 29 State 
Drug Testing Laboratories and 46 State Pharmacies h ave been set up and upgraded @ Rs.1.50 crore/DTI, a nd Rs. 2.00 
crore/pharmacy. In the Eleventh plan the scheme was  revised to include three new components of strengt hening of the State 
enforcement mechanism, upgrading the in-house testi ng facilities of manufacturing units and assisting manufacturing units 
desirous of obtaining higher GMP like EU and WHO-GMP. 
9.2  The Committee notes that inspite of major chan ges in the scheme, fund utilization status has been  far from satisfactory. 
Against an Eleventh Plan outlay of Rs.225 crore, fu nds amounting to only Rs. 45.00 crore could be allo cated during the first 
three years of the plan period and expenditure reported upto 15th March, 2010 is only Rs.26.52 crore. 

9.3  The Committee finds that out of 29 Drug Testin g Laboratories assisted financially so far, 17 labs  are established in terms 
of equipment and buildings. Other labs are in diffe rent stages of construction of building and procure ment of equipment. Only 
46 ASU&H pharmacies have been covered under the Scheme so far. 
9.4 Committee’s attention has also been drawn by th e very low number of GMP compliant ASU&H Drug manuf acturing 
units in the country. Out of total 9837 such units,  only 4663 units are GMP complying units. Ratio of GMP compliant /non-
GMP compliant units is very unsatisfactory with the  maximum gap noticed in States like Assam, Haryana,  Kerala, Madhya 
Pradesh, Maharashtra, U.P., Tamil Nadu, Uttarakhand , Punjab. As many as 2336 legal notices have been i ssued/licenses 
cancelled so far. 
9.5 The Committee has taken note of a number of cor rective measures suggested during the Mid-term Appr aisal of Eleventh 
plan. The Committee would like to emphasize that qu ality control and quality assurance are the major i ssues with reference to 
ASU drugs. The Committee, therefore, recommends tha t corrective measures as suggested in the Mid-term Appraisal may be 
initiated without delay. 
Action Taken  
 Mid term appraisal was done for the Centrally Spon sored Scheme for Quality Control of ASU&H drugs for  the effective 
implementation of the scheme. A meeting was held on  15.10.09 in the Planning Commission. Under the sch eme Rs. 2.30 erore 
has been spent till now. Other corrective measures are being taken for effective implementation. 
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE  
 This is yet another instance of casual reply by th e Department. Instead of furnishing a comprehensive  reply 
detailing the specific measures being taken/contemplated to be taken towards overcoming the shortcomings as identified 
in the mid-term appraisal, the Department has merely made a generic statement which, in the opinion of the Committee,

measures being taken for addressing the shortcoming s, especially those concerning quality control and quality

prevaricate. For example, the Committee was earlier  informed by the Department that the allocation of Rs. 25.00 crore 
in BE 2009-10 was brought down to Rs. 10.00 at RE s tage due to reduced allocation as a whole for the D epartment. The 
Department has now informed that allocation had to be reduced to Rs. 10.00 at RE stage due to inadequa te proposals 
received during the 1st half. The Committee would t herefore, like the Department to explain this ambig uity. The 
Committee also notes that against the utilization f igures of Rs. 8.57 crore as on 15th March, 2010, th e funds released 
upto 31st March, 2010 amounted to Rs. 16.54 crore. The Committee would, like the Department to indicat e the 
proposals received for funding under this head and the amount released for them, month-wise.   (Para 11.2)

 The Department has chosen to remain silent on the issue of how the funds to the tune of Rs. 66 lakhs have been 
spent when no agency was finalised to conduct the survey. The Committee would like to be apprised on this account.  
       (Para 12.3)

 The Committee observes that modifications in the e ligibility criteria for releasing grants-in-aid to AYUSH 
Educational Institutions is a positive initiative t aken by the Department. The Committee would appreci ate if all the 
procedural formalities for approval of the Scheme are completed at the earliest.   (Para 13.4)
